title: Avocado toast
intro: Crisp sourdough, lemony smashed avocado and cherry tomatoes.

steps.t: Toast the bread in a toaster or griddle pan until crisp and golden.
steps.label: Toast

steps.t: Meanwhile, mash the avocado with a fork with lemon juice, salt and pepper, keeping it a little chunky.
Halve the cherry tomatoes and dress them with a drizzle of oil and a pinch of salt.
Spread the avocado on generously, then add the tomatoes, chilli flakes, seeds and a drizzle of oil.

tips.t: Top with a poached egg or crumbled feta for a full brunch (no longer vegan).
Rub a garlic clove over the hot toast: it scents everything without overpowering the avocado.

title: Eggs Benedict
intro: Toasted muffins, ham, poached eggs and hollandaise: the brunch classic.

steps.t: Melt the butter in a small pan until hot and foaming, then keep it warm.
For the hollandaise, whisk the yolks, 1 tbsp water and lemon juice in a bowl over barely simmering water (not touching it) until thick and pale.
steps.label: Hollandaise

steps.t: Off the heat, pour in the hot butter in a thin stream, whisking constantly, until thick and glossy. Add salt and cayenne; keep over the warm water.
Bring a wide pan of water to a gentle simmer with the vinegar. Crack each egg into a small cup.
Swirl the water, slide in the eggs one at a time and poach until the whites are set and the yolks soft. Drain on paper.
steps.label: Eggs

steps.t: Meanwhile, toast the split muffins and warm the ham in a dry pan, 1 minute per side.
Top each muffin half with ham, an egg, a generous spoonful of hollandaise, chives and pepper.

tips.t: If the hollandaise splits, whisk 1 tbsp hot water in a clean bowl and gradually whisk the sauce back in.
Swap the ham for smoked salmon and you have Eggs Royale.

title: Menemen
intro: Turkish breakfast: soft scrambled eggs in a sauce of tomatoes and green peppers.

steps.t: Heat the oil in a pan and cook the chopped onion and sliced peppers over medium heat until soft.
steps.label: Peppers

steps.t: Add the peeled, chopped tomatoes, salt and pul biber and cook until saucy and most of the liquid has gone.
steps.label: Tomatoes

steps.t: Lightly beat the eggs, pour them in and stir gently a few times over low heat until just set but still creamy.
steps.label: Eggs

steps.t: Turn off the heat, scatter with parsley and serve straight from the pan with warm bread.

tips.t: Out of season, use 400 g canned peeled tomatoes: better than tasteless fresh ones.
Crumble over feta, or fry slices of sucuk (Turkish sausage) with the peppers.

title: Tamagoyaki
intro: Japanese rolled omelette in layers, sweet and savory and pillowy soft.

steps.t: Beat the eggs with chopsticks without making foam, with dashi, soy, mirin, sugar and salt, until the sugar dissolves.
Heat a rectangular tamagoyaki pan (or small non-stick pan) over medium-low heat and grease it with oiled kitchen paper.
Pour in a thin layer of egg and tilt to cover the base. When nearly set but still wet on top, roll it up towards you.
Push the roll to the far end, oil the free space, add another layer, lifting the roll so egg runs under it. Roll again and repeat.
Turn it out onto a bamboo mat or baking paper, shape into a neat block and let it set.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Cut into 2 cm slices and serve with grated daikon and a few drops of soy sauce.

tips.t: Low heat and thin layers: if the egg browns, the tamagoyaki turns rubbery.
Vegetarian version: swap the dashi for water and add a pinch more sugar.
Serve with rice, miso soup and pickles for a proper Japanese breakfast.

title: Gallo pinto
intro: Costa Rica's breakfast: day-old rice fried with black beans and pepper.

steps.t: Heat the oil in a wide pan and cook the finely chopped onion and pepper over medium heat until soft.
steps.label: Vegetables

steps.t: Add garlic and cumin for 30 seconds, then the beans with their liquid, and let it bubble.
steps.label: Beans

steps.t: Add the rice and stir-fry over medium-high heat until it's well coloured by the beans and almost dry.
steps.label: Rice

steps.t: Season with salt, stir in chopped cilantro and serve with sliced avocado.

tips.t: The rice must be cold and day-old: freshly cooked rice turns mushy.
In Costa Rica it comes with a fried egg, fried ripe plantain and a splash of Lizano sauce.
